agent_authored.description: LIANA+ infers cell-cell communication from expression: given a ligand-receptor resource and cell-type labels it scores which pairs of cell types are plausibly talking, calibrating the scores by permuting the labels. Its spatial arm computes local ligand-receptor interaction curves and bivariate spatial statistics over a neighbourhood graph, so communication can be localised in tissue rather than only summarised per cell type.

modules.title: LIANA+ — the complete cell-cell communication and spatial statistics environment (LRIC, spatial bivariate statistics, method ensemble, causal networks)
entrypoints: liana.method.sp.lric — the annulus-binned ligand-receptor interaction curve; the owned segmented reduction
liana.method.sp.bivariate — the eight local and two global bivariate spatial statistics
liana.method.rank_aggregate and the individual scoring methods (cellphonedb, natmi, connectome, logfc, singlecellsignalr, cellchat, geometric_mean)
liana.method.fun.build_prior_network and find_causalnet — the causal-network layer over corneto
liana.utils and liana.plotting — the shared preprocessing, resource and plotting surface
modules.expensive_path: Two owned numba kernels, and they are the only numba in the package. (1) src/liana/method/sp/_LRIC.py:287-315 _segment_weighted_sums, 29 lines: out[g,p] = sum over ordered spatial pairs (i,j) in group g of WL[i,p] * WR[j,p], a segmented weighted outer-product reduction over a spatial edge list, triple-loop chunked over ligand-receptor pairs, groups and edge blocks. (2) src/liana/method/sp/_bivariate/_local_functions.py:260-302 _wcorr (@nb.njit, 19 lines) and _masked_spearman (@nb.njit(parallel=True) with nb.prange, 22 lines). Together that is roughly 70 lines of owned kernel. Both sit on the same AnnData and MuData objects, the same ligand-receptor resources, the same spatial connectivity and the same preprocessing and output infrastructure.
modules.rationale: One whole-codebase module, per the curator's decision on PR #615 (2026-09-09T22:59:34Z). An earlier cut proposed two modules (spatial-lric and spatial-bivariate). Although the two methods produce different statistics, both operate on the same AnnData and MuData objects, ligand-receptor resources, spatial connectivity, preprocessing and output infrastructure. The split owned only 7 files and 2,559 lines while depending on 21 shared files and 2,058 lines, and left most of the codebase unclassified; two separate environment contracts would be thin and duplicative. A module must be an independently packageable, executable and optimisable component with its own public contract, and at this repository scale only the complete tracked tree meets that bar.
excluded: Nothing is excluded from the module boundary: paths is ['.'] and the module owns the complete tracked source tree.

No selective cap is imposed on the test surface. Every upstream pytest item and official example is in scope for the Step 2 survey; any item that cannot be carried into the task will be identified individually with its exact blocker for curator review.

src/liana/method/sp/_bivariate/ -- a different statistic (local bivariate spatial correlation over a kNN weight matrix) with its own entrypoint li.mt.bivariate and its own tests; proposed separately as spatial-bivariate
src/liana/method/sp/_inflow.py and _compute_global_specificity.py -- share the spatial-neighbours idea but not the annulus/edge-list machinery, and are mostly scipy-sparse hstack/dot delegation
src/liana/method/sp/_misty/ -- sklearn RandomForest/linear model delegation, no owned kernel
src/liana/method/sc/ and _pipe_utils/_get_mean_perms.py -- disqualified by the rapids-singlecell CUDA ligrec twin, see not_packaged
src/liana/utils/spatial_neighbors.py -- builds kNN/kernel connectivity for the bivariate and inflow paths; LRIC does not use it, it builds its own cKDTree
src/liana/multi/, src/liana/resource/, src/liana/method/fun/ -- IO, orthology, network inference; resource/ is also the package's only network surface
src/liana/utils/spatial_neighbors.py -- builds the connectivity weight matrix this module consumes; shared with inflow, so it is infrastructure rather than owned
src/liana/method/sp/_LRIC.py and its helpers -- the spatial-lric module
hazards: FRESHNESS. LRIC landed AT the pin: commit f45f7ef is literally 'Merge pull request #253 from saezlab/lric_analytical', ~13 min before v1.10.0 was published. This is the youngest API in the package and upstream still carries origin/pcf and origin/lric_analytical branches, so the surface may churn. Good for novelty (no GPU port can exist yet), a risk for pin stability.

FLOATING-POINT REASSOCIATION IS THE REAL TOLERANCE DRIVER. _segment_weighted_sums reads float32 WL/WR but accumulates into float64 via .sum(axis=0, dtype=np.float64), and the loop nest (pair chunk -> group -> edge block, with edge_block = _EDGE_BLOCK_ELEMS // n_pairs_in_chunk) pins a specific summation order. Any GPU port reassociates that reduction. Tolerances must be derived for reassociation over ~n_edges terms, not from the two-ULP variant spread, which will badly understate it.

STORED float32 VS float64 IDENTITY. Upstream comments that result columns are stored float32 while the factorisation identity holds in float64, so error tracks |g| (~1e-7 relative). Rubrics must be relative (rtol), not fixed-decimal absolute -- upstream itself switched that test from assert_array_almost_equal to assert_allclose(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6) for exactly this reason.

PLOTTING TESTS ARE WEAK CHECKS. 8 of the 57 collected tests (7 in test_lric_plot.py, 1 in test_annulus.py) are plotnine/matplotlib smoke tests returning Figure objects. They are real official tests but poor graded checks; the numeric mass is test_LRIC.py (40) plus test_lric_helpers.py (9). Count the module as ~40 genuinely gradeable, still far above the thin threshold.

THE cKDTree STEP IS DELEGATED. _support_edge_list calls scipy.spatial.cKDTree.sparse_distance_matrix (0.425 s, ~2.5%). A solver cannot port scipy, and must reproduce its exact half-open [inner, outer) binning and self-pair exclusion (I != J) or every downstream count shifts by a bin. Frame the acceleration check on _segment_weighted_sums, not on neighbour search.

ADJACENCY TO ARGUE EXPLICITLY IN THE SOURCE PR. rapids-singlecell ships _cuda/cooc/{cooc.cu,kernels_cooc.cuh}, a CUDA spatial co-occurrence kernel. It is NOT a twin -- it is cumulative-disc (dist_sq <= thresholds[r] with an inclusive scan), symmetrized (Y[i,j] and Y[j,i] both incremented), label-only with no expression term, and normalized as a conditional-probability ratio cond/col_sum rather than observed/expected pair counts per annulus. But it is close enough in spirit that a reviewer will raise it, so the distinction must be written down rather than left implicit.

use_raw DEFAULTS TO True. prep_check_adata raises ValueError('.raw is not initialized!') unless .raw is set or use_raw=False is passed. I hit this on the first profiling run. Any harness that synthesises an AnnData must set one or the other.
Investigation verdict for this codebase: GO-WITH-CAVEAT.

THE HOT OWNED PATH IS NOT THE DEFAULT PATH. Seven of the nine local statistics (_vectorized_pearson/_spearman/_cosine/_jaccard, _local_morans, _product, _norm_product) are 'weight @ x_mat' scipy-sparse matmuls, i.e. delegated. Only _masked_spearman is both owned and genuinely expensive, and it is the fallback, not the default -- the investigation measured it at 6.04 s warm on 8 threads at 5,000 spots x 300 pairs versus 0.476 s for the scipy-sparse _vectorized_spearman on identical input. An acceleration check would have to target a non-default code path, which is a weaker story than spatial-lr

PARTIAL GPU TWIN. rapids-singlecell ships squidpy_gpu/_moransi.py, _gearysc.py and _autocorr.py backed by _cuda/autocorr/, each with _run_permutations_dense/_run_permutations_sparse -- GPU Moran's I and Geary's C complete with permutation nulls. Liana's _local_morans is a bivariate local Moran (x against y across LR pairs) rather than squidpy's univariate per-gene autocorrelation, so it is a distinct statistic, but the acceleration technique (sparse weight matmul plus a permutation null on GPU) is already demonstrated upstream. This is the in-tree-partial-GPU-equivalent situation: acceptable,

NUMBA SUMMATION WORKAROUNDS IN-TREE. Two NOTE comments (_local_functions.py:299 and :339) document deliberate deviations 'due to numpy/numba sum imprecision', citing numba issue 8749. The reference itself is therefore tuned around a specific accumulator behaviour, which makes bit-level agreement with a reimplementation fragile and complicates the warrant.
The kernels are declared with explicit float32 signatures (nb.float32[:,:](...)), so dtype handling is rigid and a port must match the float32 intermediate precision, not silently promote.

DEPENDENCY PIN, corneto: pyproject.toml:65 pins corneto==0.9.1-alpha.6 exactly. Installing a newer corneto (1.0.0rc5 was tried here) breaks the three test_causalnet.py items with AttributeError: module 'corneto' has no attribute 'methods', raised from corneto/__init__.py:45 where the pre-1.0 aliases were removed. The image must honour the exact pin.

The 'network' pytest marker is registered at pyproject.toml:171 but a bare pytest run does NOT skip the items carrying it; they run. Deselecting them requires an explicit -m 'not network'. Any claim of a pass and skip partition must name the command it was measured under.

execution: CORRECTION. An earlier report interpreted 231 collected as 222 passed plus 9 skipped. That was an inference, not a measurement, and it is wrong in both directions: a bare run skips nothing and passes all 231, and the 9 items marked network are deselected only when an explicit marker expression asks for it.

Environment: CPython 3.12 in a fresh venv. liana 1.10.0 installed from the clean tracked checkout with --no-deps --no-build-isolation. Runtime dependencies from pyproject plus the extras group, with corneto==0.9.1-alpha.6 exactly as pyproject.toml line 65 pins it. Full freeze recorded in the raw log.
RUN 1, command: python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly, network reachable. Result: 231 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 97.26 s. Nothing is skipped by a bare run.

RUN 2, command: python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly -m 'not network', network reachable. Result: 222 passed, 9 deselected, 0 failed, 85.96 s. The 9 network items are DESELECTED, not skipped, and only when the marker expression is given.

RUN 3, command: unshare -rn python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly, no network namespace at all. Result: 229 passed, 2 failed, 88.06 s. The two failures are tests.resource.test_resource_utils.test_generate_lr_resource and test_generate_nondefault_lr_resource, both URL fetches. So only 2 of the 9 network-marked items actually require the network in this environment.
RUN 4, command: unshare -rn python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly -m 'not network'. Result: 222 passed, 9 deselected, 0 failed, 88.29 s. This is the offline-clean configuration.
Accounting is consistent across all four: 231 collected = 222 non-network + 9 network.

Dependency pin that matters: installing a newer corneto (1.0.0rc5 was tried) fails the three test_causalnet.py items with AttributeError: module 'corneto' has no attribute 'methods', raised at corneto/__init__.py line 45 where the pre-1.0 aliases were removed. The image must honour the exact pin.
No selective cap is imposed. All 231 items are in scope for the Step 2 survey; any item that cannot be carried into the task will be named individually with its exact blocker.

BRIEF IS WRONG AT THIS PIN: src/liana/method/_pipe_utils/_get_mean_perms.py contains no numba, no njit, no prange and no raw-CSR indexing at v1.10.0. It is 186 lines of numpy + joblib.Parallel and imports neither numba nor scipy.sparse. grep -rn 'njit|prange|numba' src returns hits in exactly one file. Whoever wrote the hazard note was reading an older revision; do not scaffold a module around a k

The only numba in the package is 41 lines (_wcorr + _masked_spearman, _bivariate/_local_functions.py:260-302). If the task premise is 'port the owned numba kernels', the honest owned-kernel surface is 41 lines, which is far below any merged leaf. The defensible expensive path is _segment_weighted_sums in _LRIC.py, which is numpy, not numba.

rapids-singlecell 0.16.1 ships a real CUDA CellPhoneDB permutation kernel (_cuda/ligrec/ligrec.cu + kernels_ligrec.cuh, 433 lines, behind squidpy_gpu/_ligrec.py). It is not an API drop-in for liana, but it computes the same statistic as li.mt.cellphonedb. The single-cell LR-methods module (module C) should not be the acceleration target. Choose spatial-lric.
_liana_pipe.py:307 calls scanpy's sc.tl.rank_genes_groups, for which rapids-singlecell has a CUDA Wilcoxon (_cuda/wilcoxon/). Second, independent delegation disqualifier for module C.

_misty/_single_view_models.py delegates to sklearn RandomForestRegressor , LinearRegression , cross_val_predict and statsmodels OLS; multi/_nmf.py to sklearn NMF; utils/spatial_neighbors.py to sklearn NearestNeighbors. cuML drop-ins exist for all of these. Not module material.

The bivariate statistics other than masked_spearman are scipy-sparse matmuls (weight @ x_mat); cupyx.scipy.sparse is a literal drop-in, so an acceleration-labelled check on module B must be masked_spearman specifically, not morans/pearson/cosine.

Nine tests are @pytest.mark.network (tests/resource/test_get_metalinks.py x4, test_orthology.py x3, test_resource_utils.py x2). They hit MetaLinksDB and the HCOP orthology table and cache under tests/.cache. They are the entire download surface and must be excluded from any check set with -m 'not network'.

li.testing.kang_2018() pulls ~200 MB from figshare into the working directory on first call. It is never called by the test suite but IS used by the docs notebooks, so do not derive a check from a notebook.
open_questions: Determinism as measured: Bitwise reproducible on every path measured -- unusually good for a permutation-heavy package. - cellphonedb, 700x765, n_perms=100, seed=1337: rerun with the same seed is bitwise identical on all six float columns (ligand_means, ligand_props, receptor_means, receptor_props, lr_means, cellphone_pvals), AND n_jobs=1 vs n_jobs=4 is bitwise identical. Structural reason: `_generate_perms_cube` draws `rng.permutation(idx)` in the generator on the main thread and joblib only carries the resulting index

Recommended first module: PACKAGE spatial-lric FIRST. It is the only candidate where the expensive path is simultaneously owned, dominant, and untwinned -- and I established each of those by running something rather than reading. OWNED AND DOMINANT. cProfile on one li.mt.lric call at 12,000 cells , 600 LR pairs puts _segment_weighted_sums (_LRIC.py:287-315, 29 lines) at 12.527 s tottime and 14.842 s cumtime of a 16.568 s wall -- 90% cumulative -- with its own .sum(axis=0, dtype=np.float64) as the only other top entry a
